# TOTP

> **Domain:** [[04 - Identity and Access Management|Identity & Access Management]]
> **Also known as:** Time-based One-Time Password, HOTP, OTP

**T**ime-based **O**ne-**T**ime **P**assword. A 6–8 digit code derived from a shared secret and the current time (30-second windows), as generated by authenticator apps. **HOTP** is the counter-based predecessor.

**Context.** TOTP is the workhorse second factor: open standard, offline, works in any authenticator app (and in [[KeePassXC]]-style managers). Its weakness is phishability — the code can be relayed in real time by a proxy phishing kit, which is exactly what [[FIDO2 and WebAuthn]] was designed to fix. Still vastly better than SMS codes, which add SIM-swapping to the threat list.

## Often confused with

- [[Passkey]] — TOTP is a shared-secret code you type (phishable); a passkey is an unphishable public-key credential bound to the site's origin.
